text:
maria: Heads up — after last night's CUDA 535.101 driver rollout in us-west-2 inference pool, ~10% of TensorRT/FlashAttention jobs are hanging in the generation step. Repro: single-request sync gen stalls for 30-120s then resume. Logs show kernels stuck on memcopy/NCCL errors.

todd: ugh. which nodes? driver/kernel versions?

maria: nodes: inf-gpu-4-*-usw2 (mixed A100S and A10G). Driver: 535.101.02. Linux: 5.15.0-88-generic. Container base: ubuntu22.04. Model runtime: TRT 8.4.3 + flash-attn wheel 2.0. Snippet:

```
[flashattn] launch failed: CUDA error 700 (an illegal memory access was encountered)
[trt] Error: NCCL kernel allreduce failed: unhandled CUDA error
```

sophia: can you paste nvidia-smi and dmesg around the time? also did you see GPU reset events?

maria: nvidia-smi and dmesg pasted below (excerpt):

```
GPU 0: A100S 40GB - persistence-mode: Enabled
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                                      GPU Memory|
|  0    21452  C      python /app/server.py                                 32000MiB|
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
[  +0.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=21452, 0e: ...
[  +0.001234] nvc: nvidia: unhandled page fault at ...
```

infra-bot: probe/healthcheck results for cluster 'inference-usw2': 12% of nodes reported 'hang' signal after 02:00 maintenance. Canary subset hit 3/50 nodes.

jonas: sounds like a kernel ABI mismatch with FlashAttention/TensorRT cuda kernels. Did we rebuild wheels after driver upgrade? xformers/flash-attn ABI is fragile.

maria: we didn't rebuild — upgrade was driver-only. quick workaround: forcing fallback to non-fused kernels helps (set REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_ATTENTION=1). With that, jobs run but cost + latency up ~25%.

kevin: try setting CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get a backtrace, but that will reduce perf. Also try LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so to see if it exposes a different error. Also collect core dumps from the container.

sophia: we should roll driver back in canary and stop the full rollout. todd: can you taint new nodes and repro on isolated pool?

todd: on it. taint applied to nodes matching inference-usw2-canary. scheduling new canary with driver 535.86 rollback. will update.

maria: FYI workaround env var above + restarting TRT engines reduces frequency to <1%. But ops prefers rollback.

oncall: opened incident INC-2026-1137, priority=P2. Assigning eng-infra + eng-runtime.

jonas: long-term fix: rebuild flash-attn and xformers wheels against 535.101 toolchain + TRT 8.5? Need CI job matrix across driver versions. Also consider shipping multi-kernel fallback in runtime.

maria: agreed. I'll add a postmortem checklist: 1) stop rollout, 2) rollback canary, 3) reproduce with debug env, 4) rebuild wheels + validate on canary, 5) resume.

kevin: adding note — NCCL ABI/driver combos sometimes change memalign behaviour; also check libgcc/libstdc++ versions inside container.

maria: thanks all. I'll post status when rollback complete. :thumbsup:
